description: Small, reviewable additions to the historical Growth Library index. scripts/apply-content-additions.mjs merges these records into data/life-os-content/index.json before build/check so agents do not need to replace the 20k+ line legacy index for each new reviewed protocol.

entries.title: Batch Non-Urgent Notifications Instead of Receiving Them All Day
entries.subtitle: Make interruptions predictable without pretending every alert should disappear
entries.description: Group non-urgent smartphone notifications into a few predictable delivery windows while keeping genuinely urgent channels available. The useful idea is predictable batching, not a magic number of batches.

entries.title: Check Email in Deliberate Windows Instead of Continuously
entries.subtitle: Reduce inbox switching without pretending every role can ignore email
entries.description: If constant inbox checking fragments your day, test a few deliberate email windows and close the inbox between them. Match the schedule to real response expectations rather than copying a fixed number from a study.

entries.title: Make Your Phone Less Visually Tempting with Grayscale
entries.subtitle: A reversible interface nudge for reducing habitual screen time
entries.description: If you want to spend less time on your phone, try switching the display to grayscale for a bounded trial. Treat it as friction against habitual use, not as a productivity, sleep, or mental-health upgrade.

entries.title: Walk Soon After a Meal When You Would Otherwise Sit
entries.subtitle: A simple movement option with an acute post-meal glucose signal
entries.description: When it is safe and practical, replace some sitting after a meal with comfortable walking. Evidence supports an acute effect on post-meal glucose, not a universal walking dose or long-term treatment claim.

entries.title: Pause Long Enough to Notice a Good Moment
entries.subtitle: A small savoring practice without forced positivity
entries.description: When something genuinely pleasant is already happening, give it a little deliberate attention instead of rushing past it. This is a conservative savoring practice, not a rule to feel positive or reinterpret difficult experiences.
